question: How frequent is the existing verified arithmetic-boundary class at naturally selected bounded prediction positions, rather than in documents selected to contain calculations?
positions: Every bounded native-token cut 512..min(8192,L-16), regardless of equals signs, label, serialization rejection, or expression novelty; past512/future16.
estimands: Exact finite-frame position-weighted verified incidence, sum(k)/sum(n)
Exact document-balanced expected random-cut incidence, mean(k/n) among complete-window documents
Document contains at least one verified full-prefix boundary; distinct denominator
One identity/length-hash-selected cut per eligible document, fixed independently of candidate validity
The same counts after removing all original cohort source identities
limits: Only the pinned source-clean16-shard TRAIN frame and original bounded curator definition; not all FineMath, general language, or every kind of useful computation.

Verified class uses source RHS to label correctness, never to choose a prospective random position. Auxiliary packing and expression-novelty checks are not applied, so incidence precedes those further restrictions.
Pre-label-stage incidence includes native whole-window serialization checks that can depend on future text. It is not a qualified causal invocation policy.
No confidence interval is needed for exact incidence in this finite frame. These counts alone do not establish natural-corpus predictive gains or transport the selected ordinary-panel costs.
Prior source-level curation counts and a few audit rows were inspected; no predictive scores or new population prevalence counts were consulted to set this design.
